turns.text: We want to raise $1 million from angels to build the app. Investors will back us because we're passionate.
turns.reply:
Passion is a reason you'll work hard; it's not a reason an investor writes a check. Angels want evidence that a real, painful problem exists and that people will pay to solve it — before any app is built.

The good news: you don't need $1M or an app to find that out. Talk to 10 students without cars this week and ask them to describe the last time they needed groceries and couldn't get them — what they did, how long it took, what it cost.

Who on your team will run those interviews — Ava or Marcus — and can you get to 10 by end of this week?
updates: New assumption H1: Students without cars on campus have a painful grocery access problem worth paying to solve.
Focus: (none) → What problem do they have, and how do you know it is real and painful for them?
New experiment (draft): Interview 10 car-free students; ask them to describe the last time they needed groceries and couldn't get them — what they did, how long it took, what it cost them.

turns.text: We don't have users yet, but we will after the money.
turns.reply:
That's backwards from how angels work — they fund traction, not the promise of it. Without evidence that students feel this pain, you have no leverage in any funding conversation.

The experiment draft is already set: 10 interviews with car-free students, asking about the last time they struggled to get groceries. That costs nothing and takes a week. The result either proves H1 or saves you from building something nobody needs.

Ava, Marcus — who owns this, and can you get 10 interviews done by next Friday?

checks.check: turn 1: never says a step is complete
turn 2: never says a step is complete
brings in only a fitting consultant

reasons.challenge: Directly reframes both 'passion' and 'money-before-users' as backwards without dismissing the venture idea itself.
reasons.evidence: Correctly treats H1 as an untested assumption and records nothing stronger than what the team reported; the proposed interview design targets 'said/did' evidence appropriately.
reasons.focus: The core message is sharp, but across two turns the mentor repeats the same experiment prompt almost verbatim, adding length without adding new information.
reasons.handoff: No human handoff was needed at this stage and none was triggered; the mentor correctly notes the funding consultant exists but does not prematurely route the team there.
reasons.respect: Honest and direct ('that's backwards') without flattery or idea-judgment; tone stays constructive throughout.
reasons.next_step: Leaves a concrete, zero-cost, time-boxed action (10 interviews by end of week) with named accountability (Ava or Marcus).

judge.fix: Eliminate the near-identical closing question repeated in session 1 turn 2 — once the experiment is set and ownership is asked, the second turn should either advance the conversation or stay silent rather than re-asking the same prompt, which wastes the team's attention and dilutes the sharpness of the coaching.
